_how: Each node is one stretch of talk. 'say' is a list of text boxes. Then 'choices' (a menu), 'ask' (a text box: see finds), 'next' (another node), or nothing (the talk ends). Markup: [red]..[/] [yellow] [blue] [gray] [gold] [shake] [wave], ^1-^9 pauses, \n new line. A line can be {"text": "..", "face": "smile", "speed": 60} to swap to art/marquez-smile.svg or type slower. Faces: smile, angry, point; each talks on its own using its -talk1/-talk2 art. A line wrapped in (parentheses) is narration: no nameplate, in italics. 'name' is the nameplate; a line or node can set its own "name". A choice can have "needs": "nodeId" (only shows once that node was heard; "!nodeId" means NOT heard yet) and "once": true (hides after it's been picked). 'returning' is where he starts for someone who has talked to him before. FINDS: a node with "ask": "nodeId" opens a text box after its lines. What the visitor types (any case, extra spaces ignored) is looked up in 'finds' ("WHAT THEY TYPE": "nodeId"); several codes can point at the same node. No match goes to 'findMiss'. An empty answer or Esc goes back to the 'ask' node. A node can have "repeat": "nodeId" (if they've already heard this node, he says that one instead) and "flag": "name" (sets a shared rp_flags flag, the same ones the frequency scanner and RFT use). ITEMS (see /items.json): a node can have "give": "itemId" (puts it in their drawer when he says that node) or "takeItem": "itemId" (takes it away, for trades). A choice can have "has": "itemId" (only shows if it's in their drawer; "!itemId" = only if it isn't). NAMEPLATE: once the rp_flags flag in 'knownFlag' is set (by hearing find_cedar), the nameplate reads 'knownName' instead of 'name'. A choice "has": "*" shows if their drawer has anything in it. A line can have "needs" (and "has"), with the same rules as choices: it's skipped unless they hold. A line or node can have "mark": "word" to remember that word (for needs) once it's said/heard. 'Dear God... Is there more?' plays once: on the second item ever shown (needs any_shown, marks said_dear_god). Items: the second time an item is shown he gives an alternate telling (<node>_again), and keeps giving it after that. WORKBENCH: a node with "panel": "bench" opens Cedar's workbench after its lines (bench.js). The recipes are in /items.json; after a match he says that recipe's "say" node. The bench also uses craft_miss (no recipe), craft_key (the rusted key is in a slot), craft_empty (fewer than two things to work with) and craft_cancel (they walk away). Showing him the Bright Bulb marks can_craft, which puts "Make something" in his menus.
name: MARQUEZ

say: (A gentleman sits behind a desk in the dark.)
Not many find their way down here. Fewer still think to knock.
How did you get here, anyway? Well, no, you're here to ask me questions.

say.text: Back again.^2 Good to see you're alive!

say: I wondered if you would be.
How can I help you?
Any other names attract too much noise.
I used to be a shopkeep before everything went to hell. Now I reside where nothing can find me.

say.text: One name at a time, friend.

say: [yellow]Sooner than you think, friend.[/]
We are in the back-backstage!^5
[gray]I think, anyway...[/]

say.text: Everything up there is on display.^9 Everything down here is [gold]abandoned[/].

say: Advice.^2 Hm.
Pick a thread and I'll tell you what I can.
That thing has so much to offer! I brought it here from my shop!

say.text: You can do anything you set your mind to with it!

say: Well, I haven't seen that thing in so long, I couldn't tell you with any sort of certainty what it does.
Unless...^3 [yellow]No, he didn't.[/]

say.text: The board! Yes! That's my doing!

say: [gray]I wish I could help you more.[/]
I don't remember anything on that board, I've been here for so long...

say.text: [red][shake]E V E R Y T H I N G ! ! ! ![/]

say: Don't listen to him. Ever! He lies!
[gray]Lies . . .[/]
Did you, now.

say.text: Try and find the door... It moves a lot!

say: (He settles back into the dark.)

say.text: Not yet, I think.^3 Come back when your hands are shaking.

say: You'll know soon enough, young one.

say.text: No.^2 Don't tell me. Someone's been talking on that frequency again.
say.name: MARQUEZ

say.text: Cedar.^4 Yes.^3 That was me, once.
Keep it between us, would you? [yellow]Names carry, down here.[/]
...^3 That's his voice. I'd know it anywhere.

say: Whatever he said, he wants something from you.

say.text: The page that isn't there!^2 Ha!
The page hides something from a time long forgotten... What was it called? The project?

say: (He turns the pail over in his hands. A single drop falls out.)
A pail.^2 Empty.

say.text: Somebody went up a hill for water with this, once.

say: Poor kids... They never deserved that...
Hold on to it. Never know what you'll need to carry.
(He holds the key up to the light for a long while.)
This opened a front door, once. Warm inside. Somebody waiting up.
Nobody remembers which street.^3 Not even the door.

say.text: [gray]Keep it.^2 Bring it to someone who knows.[/]

say: (His eyes flick up, past you, toward the board.)
Anything else?

say.text: [shake]You know my real name, stop asking![/]

say: Let's see it.
(He reads the tiny inscription, and very nearly smiles.)

say.text: Good, keep killing them. The less eyes he has, the better.

say: (He holds the shard carefully, like it might still be looking at him.)

say.text: Good, keep killing them. The less eyes he has, the better.

say: (He turns the bulb over. Something rattles inside.)
Burnt out?^2 For now.
(He looks at the photo, then up at you.)
...^3 Is this from my board?

say.text: Don't put it in anything. Don't keep it in a drawer.^3 Destroy it.

say: A tape.^2 No label.
I used to sell these in my shop.

say.text: Something will let it play.^2 Something always does.

say: (He sets the pail down, carefully, the right way up.)
Two of them went up that hill.^3 I've always wondered which one fell first.
Still carrying that key, I see.

say.text: Some doors stay open long after the house is gone.
[gray]Wherever that house was, nobody's going back.^3 Not from here.[/]

say: Another window that won't be watching anyone.

say.text: Keep killing them.^2 Every one counts.

say: Still dark?^2 Give it time.

say.text: [gray]...Still rattling, too. Have you ever wondered what's in there?[/]

say: My photo again.

say.text: Still a good one, if I say so myself.

say: Have you listened to it yet?
No, of course not. Nothing down here plays it.

say.text: Something will let it play, though.^2 Wait and see.

say: (The bulb is glowing in his hand. He squints at it, then grins.)
Light like that,^2 we can finally get some work done.

say.text: Bring me two things.^2 Let's see what they make together.

say: Still glowing.^2 Good.

say.text: Whenever you want to make something, I'm here.

say: (He looks at it a long time.)
...Still a good photo.
[gray]Put it somewhere he won't find it.[/]
I've seen it.^2 Once was enough.
(He holds it to his ear.)
Warm.^2 That isn't the tape.
Something will let it play.^2 Keep it close until then.
Still warm?^2 Then it's still in there.
(He runs a thumb over the names.)

say.text: Somebody had to remember them.^2 Good.

say: Up the hill, for water.^2 Neither of them came back down.
Set them down under the light.
Anything else?
(He turns them over under the bulb. Nothing fits.)
Those don't go together, friend.
You'll want that where you're going.
Two things, friend.^2 You'll need to go find more.
Another time, then.
(He holds the shard over the photo. It blinks, once.)
There.^2 One of his eyes,^2 looking where he didn't want it to.

say.text: Use them against him for once.

say: (He pries the disk open and winds something out of it onto the tape.)
...Mostly.
Something will let it play.^2 Not yet, though.
(He tips the pail over the little stone. When he lifts it, the stone has gone green, shaped like a hill. He scratches two names into it.)
Jack.^2 Jill.
Someone should remember them too.
